# 45 Recto

The throngs of perfected ones <term>Siddhas</term> <gloss>perfected masters</gloss> and the liberated ones are praising you with sublime hymns. The <term>Rudras</term> <gloss>manifestations of Shiva</gloss>, the <term>Adityas</term> <gloss>solar deities</gloss>, the <term>Vasus</term> <gloss>elemental gods</gloss>, and the <term>Sadhyas</term> <gloss>celestial guardians</gloss>, the <term>Vishvedevas</term> <gloss>universal gods</gloss>, the two <term>Ashvins</term> <gloss>divine physicians</gloss>, the <term>Maruts</term> <gloss>storm gods</gloss>, and the <term>Ushmapas</term> <gloss>ancestral spirits</gloss>. 22.

The hosts of <term>Gandharvas</term> <gloss>celestial musicians</gloss>, <term>Yakshas</term> <gloss>nature spirits</gloss>, <term>Asuras</term> <gloss>titans</gloss>, and <term>Siddhas</term> <gloss>perfected beings</gloss> are all gazing upon you in amazement. 23.

<note>The text describes Arjuna's overwhelming vision of Krishna's cosmic form, where all classes of divine and semi-divine beings are visible within a single body.</note>

Seeing your great form, with many mouths and eyes, O mighty-armed one, with many thighs, feet, and bellies, and many terrible teeth, the worlds are terrified, and so am I. 24.

Touching the sky, glowing with many colors, with mouths gaping wide and large shining eyes, seeing you, my innermost soul is trembling with fear, and I find no steady courage or peace, O Vishnu. 25. 

Seeing your mouths, terrible with tusks and resembling the fire of cosmic destruction <term>Kalanalasannibham</term> <gloss>like the fire at the end of time</gloss>.

---

# 45 Verso

I do not know the directions, nor do I find any comfort. Have mercy, O Lord of the gods, O Refuge of the universe. 26.

<note>The following sections contain repetitive invocations and corrupted OCR strings that appear to be ritualistic praises or scribal notations regarding fame and devotion.</note>

Here, Sudhama, the servant of the servants, whose fame is without end. Among the hosts of gods, the joy of the world remains. Here, Sudhama, the servant of the servants, whose fame is without end. 

The fearful forms of the Great Work are encountered. Without fame, the gods are lost. 

Now, through the sacrifice, the ruler is equalized. 21. Just as there is joy in the abode of the sun. 22. 

Here, Sudhama, the servant of the servants, whose fame is without end. The light of the mind and other faculties are broad and great. 23. Here, Sudhama, the servant of the servants, whose fame is without end.

<note>A circular hole is carved in the center of the palm leaf to allow a binding cord to pass through the stack of manuscripts.</note>

<summary>This page describes Arjuna's terrifying vision of the cosmic form of Krishna, listing the various celestial beings who witness it. The verso side includes repetitive devotional phrases and mentions the scribe or patron Sudhama.</summary>
<keywords>Vishnu, Rudras, Adityas, Gandharvas, cosmic form, Vishvarupa, Sudhama, palm leaf manuscript</keywords>
